description.en:
A topic-wise e-book on Indian Polity and the Constitution for competitive exams — the making of the Constitution, Fundamental Rights and Duties, the Union and State governments, the judiciary, and the special provisions for Assam such as the Sixth Schedule and the Autonomous Councils.

This is an online reading e-book only. It cannot be downloaded as a PDF.
description.as:
প্ৰতিযোগিতামূলক পৰীক্ষাৰ বাবে ভাৰতীয় ৰাজনীতি আৰু সংবিধানৰ বিষয়-ভিত্তিক ই-বুক — সংবিধান নিৰ্মাণ, মৌলিক অধিকাৰ আৰু কৰ্তব্য, কেন্দ্ৰীয় আৰু ৰাজ্য চৰকাৰ, ন্যায়পালিকা, আৰু অসমৰ বাবে বিশেষ ব্যৱস্থা যেনে ষষ্ঠ অনুসূচী আৰু স্বায়ত্তশাসিত পৰিষদসমূহ।

এই ই-বুক কেৱল অনলাইন পঠনৰ বাবে। ইয়াক PDF হিচাপে ডাউনলোড কৰিব নোৱাৰি।

content.en:
The Indian Constitution was framed by the Constituent Assembly which was set up under the Cabinet Mission Plan of 1946. Dr. Rajendra Prasad was the President of the Assembly, and Dr. B.R. Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee and is therefore called the Father of the Indian Constitution.

The Constitution was adopted on 26 November 1949 and came into force on 26 January 1950, the day we celebrate as Republic Day. It borrowed features from many constitutions — parliamentary government from Britain, Fundamental Rights from the USA, Directive Principles from Ireland, and the federal structure with a strong centre from Canada.

The Preamble declares India to be a Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic Republic and assures justice, liberty, equality and fraternity to all citizens. The Constitution originally had 395 Articles and 8 Schedules; today it has grown through amendments to over 440 Articles and 12 Schedules.

title.as: মৌলিক অধিকাৰ, কৰ্তব্য আৰু ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় নীতি নিৰ্দেশনা

content.en:
Fundamental Rights are guaranteed in Part III of the Constitution (Articles 12–35) to protect the liberty of citizens. The six categories are: Right to Equality (Articles 14–18), Right to Freedom (19–22), Right against Exploitation (23–24), Right to Freedom of Religion (25–28), Cultural and Educational Rights (29–30), and the Right to Constitutional Remedies (32), which Dr. Ambedkar called the heart and soul of the Constitution.

Fundamental Duties were added by the 42nd Amendment (1976) on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee. Article 51A lists eleven duties of citizens, such as respecting the national flag and the Constitution and protecting the environment.

The Directive Principles of State Policy in Part IV are guidelines for the state to establish a just social order. They include the provision of free and compulsory education for children, equal pay for equal work and the organisation of village panchayats. Though not enforceable by courts, they are fundamental in the governance of the country.

title.as: কেন্দ্ৰীয়, ৰাজ্য আৰু অসমৰ ষষ্ঠ অনুসূচী

content.en:
India follows a parliamentary system with a President as the constitutional head. The real executive power lies with the Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers. The Parliament consists of the President, the Lok Sabha (House of the People) and the Rajya Sabha (Council of States). At the state level, the Governor is the constitutional head and the Chief Minister is the real executive head.

Article 356 (President's Rule) and Article 360 (Financial Emergency) are important emergency-related provisions. The independent judiciary, headed by the Supreme Court, is the guardian of the Constitution and has the power of judicial review.

For Assam and the other north-eastern states, the Sixth Schedule of the Constitution is very important. It provides for Autonomous District Councils to protect the interests of the tribal people in areas such as the Karbi Anglong, Dima Hasao and the hill districts of neighbouring states. In 2003 the Bodoland Territorial Council was created by an amendment to protect the Bodo community, and in 2020 the Karbi Anglong Agreement was signed for greater autonomy and development.
